A1.justification: Both PDFs describe ConceptAttention, with matching core formulations and experiments. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: V1 reports original ImageNet-Segmentation and PascalVOC evaluations, architectural ablations, and qualitative saliency results in Section 5 and Appendix B.

after.justification: V2 retains those empirical results and adds Stable Diffusion 3.5 results in Table 1, video experiments, and qualitative failure cases.

M1.justification: V2 introduces a limited video adaptation: Section 5.1 explicitly states that CogVideoX additionally requires averaging over the frame dimension. The image attention procedure, residual stream, saliency computation, and Appendix A pseudocode remain unchanged.

E1.justification: The ImageNet-Segmentation and PascalVOC tasks remain. V2 extends evaluation to saliency localization in generated CogVideoX video sequences (Figures 8, 16, and 17), introducing temporal inputs beyond still images. Figure 15 also tests a scenario where the correct concept is absent from the candidate vocabulary.

E2.justification: Table 1 adds CLIPasRNN, OVAM, DINOv2 SA, DINOv2 Reg SA, iBOT SA, and SD3.5 cross attention. Original numerical comparators remain, including DINO Attention renamed DINO SA. The shortened qualitative comparison drops its DINO column, while the multiclass PascalVOC comparator set is unchanged.

E3.justification: The retained benchmarks preserve their splits, metrics, mean-threshold and multiclass argmax procedures, and Flux layer/timestep choices. Added evaluations introduce SD3.5 Turbo configurations, qualitative CogVideoX frame comparisons, and a controlled comparison with versus without 'bike' in the candidate vocabulary.

E4.justification: V2 adds targeted qualitative failure analyses: overlapping concepts produce ambiguous boundaries in Figure 6, and Figure 15 tests removal of the correct concept. The original layer-depth, noise-timestep, representation-space, softmax, and attention-operation ablations are retained despite renumbering and merged displays.

E5.justification: Tables continue to report single scores, and the same shaded layer/timestep curves are retained. Neither version specifies seeds, repeated-run counts, or significance-testing procedures; v2 introduces no new uncertainty-reporting practice.

E6.justification: Matched numerical results, including the ablations and multiclass scores, are unchanged. Table 1 adds seven rows, including SD3.5 ConceptAttention with ImageNet mIoU 67.47 and mAP 90.79; these are additional backbone results, not improvements to the retained Flux scores. Video and failure-case outputs are added, while several older qualitative examples are removed.

T1.justification: The rectified-flow preliminaries, attention and residual equations, saliency definition, and layer averaging remain mathematically equivalent. V1's three projection equations are consolidated into v2 Equation 4. No new formal assumptions, theorems, proofs, or derivations appear.

C1.justification: The abstract and contribution list extend the claimed scope from image interpretation and segmentation to video-generation DiTs, explicitly claiming higher-quality video saliency maps than native cross attention. They also emphasize replication across Flux and SD3.5 Turbo. The original training-free, output-space saliency claims remain.

C2.justification: Section 5.5 newly qualifies applicability: similar concepts can have unclear boundaries, and omitting the correct vocabulary entry can assign an object's saliency to an incorrect related label. These limitations are illustrated in Figures 6 and 15. Existing interpretations of layers, noise, and attention operations are retained.

D1.justification: Section 5.1 names the additional SD3.5 Turbo and CogVideoX models and discloses frame-dimension averaging. Existing Flux implementation details and Appendix A pseudocode remain. The introductory direct repository link is removed, while the code project-page link is retained.

R1.justification: V2 adds references for CLIP as RNN, OVAM, DINOv2, registers, iBOT, and CogVideoX, while largely preserving the related-work framing. OVAM attribution is internally inconsistent: the baseline discussion cites Li et al., 2023b, whereas Table 1 cites Marcos-Manchon et al., 2024.

P1.justification: Most exposition and the conclusion remain substantially unchanged. V2 locally revises the abstract, contributions, and baseline discussion; promotes implementation details to Section 5.1; and adds video-results and limitations subsections plus Appendix C. There are also minor heading, author-name, and publication-header edits.

P2.justification: V2 redraws Figure 2, trims Figure 3 and the main qualitative comparison, expands Table 1, merges the layer/timestep plots, and adds SD3.5, failure-case, and video figures. The elephant appendix comparison is removed. Figure 4 also reverses its Raw Scores/Preds row labels relative to the displayed contents and caption.

improvement.justification: V1's broad applicability claims rested on experiments with Flux. V2 supplies quantitative SD3.5 replication, broader baseline comparisons, and qualitative video transfer, while documenting concrete failure conditions. Together these substantially strengthen empirical support and clarify applicability. Video validation remains qualitative, and minor citation and labeling errors temper but do not outweigh these gains.
